text:
MPC stock fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as refineries operate at peak capacity (97.5%) while oil storage sits at elevated levels (692 million barrels). When refineries are already running flat-out and crude inventories build up, it signals weak downstream demand—refiners have less pricing power and face tighter margins because they can't process more oil even if prices look attractive.

The broader backdrop isn't helping either. Climate talks collapsed without committing to phase out fossil fuels, which removes near-term regulatory pressure on oil demand but also reflects weak confidence in future energy transition. At the same time, news around alternative energy infrastructure (quantum computing for grids, hydrogen catalysts) and rising AI energy demand suggests money is flowing toward new energy sectors, potentially pulling investor interest away from traditional refining plays already facing margin compression from oversupply.
